raw_case_text:
A 59-year-old Indian female presented to our hospital, with c/o abdominal distension for last 2 months, generalized weakness, productive cough, and purpuric rashes over both lower limbs and fever for 2 days. The patient was a known hypertensive and hypothyroid on medications and past history of cholecystectomy 17 years back.
She was recently diagnosed as a case of chronic liver disease due to autoimmune hepatitis 3 months back was being treated for the same. She was started on wysolone 60 mg for last 3 months and azoran 100 mg for past 1 month.
On general examination, she was conscious, oriented, and afebrile. Physical examination revealed pallor, pedal edema, palpable purpuric spots on both the lower limbs. Her blood pressure was low (80/50 mm of Hg), progesterone receptor - 118/min, and risk ratio - 20/min. Chest examination revealed bilateral normal air entry with basal crepitations. Abdomen was distended and tender with sluggish bowel sounds.
Initial laboratory investigation confirmed anemia (hemoglobin - 9.3 g/dl), total lung capacity 8.9 x 109/L with neutrophilia, (neutrophil - 83%, lymphocyte - 11%, and eosinophil - 1%), and platelets 139 x 109/L.
Her kidney function were deranged - urea 120 mg/dl, creatinine 2.08 mg/dl, sodium 133 mmol/L, and potassium 4.39 mmol/L. Liver function tests were also deranged, (total bilirubin - 1.4 mg/dl, aspartate aminotransferase - 98 IU/L, alanine aminotransferase - 82 IU/L, serum alkaline phosphatase - 519 IU/L, gamma glutamyl transferase - 800 IU/L, albumin - 2.0 g/dl, and globulin - 3.3 g/dl).
Arterial blood gas revealed respiratory acidosis and lactate 3.2 (pH - 7.30, HCO3 - 20 mm Hg, PCO2 - 46 mm Hg, and PO2 -87 mm Hg.) C reactive protein 144 mg/L, because of the worsening respiratory status and altered sensorium she was intubated and put on a mechanical ventilator. She also had paralytic ileus (high RT aspirate 600 ml/24 h).
Chest X-ray showed bilateral fluffy alveolar opacities with infiltrates, left side consolidation and right homogenous opacities with ground glass appearance. Baseline ECHO with 50%, no regional wall motion abnormality, inferior vena cava 20. Ultrasonography showed liver with irregular outlines and coarse echotexture, minimal interloop ascites, few dilated fluid filled small bowel loops were seen with sluggish peristaltic movement.
Cytologic examination of the bronchial wash and lavage comprised benign respiratory epithelial cells, few polymorphs and histiocytes over hemorrhagic background. A wet mount was seen which revealed motile larvae resembling larvae of Strongyloides stercoralis [Figures 1-4].
Interestingly bronchoalveolar lavage culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae. Other cultures were sterile. CMV DNA quant 1.81 x 106/ml.
Absolute eosinophil count was -55/cumm (reference range 40-440) Serum immunoglobulin E was 319 (reference range 100). Skin biopsy showed occasional thrombi in dermal vessels with extravasation of red blood cells; epidermis was largely unremarkable which is compatible with purpura fulminans. No larvae were seen.
Antibiotics were added as per sensitivity reports. Ivermectin 12 mg once daily was added. A high ionotropic support was given to maintain mean arterial pressure of 65 mmHg.
She had a sudden onset of cardiac arrest and despite best possible effort. She could not be revived. Postmortem liver biopsy features were consistent with liver cirrhosis with features of sepsis. Muscle biopsy showed transversely and longitudinally cut muscle fibers with a focal group of atrophic muscles.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 59-year-old Indian female with autoimmune hepatitis presented with a 2-month history of abdominal distension and generalized weakness, accompanied by 2 days of productive cough, fever, and bilateral lower-extremity purpuric rashes.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed 3 months prior with chronic liver disease secondary to autoimmune hepatitis and treated with oral prednisolone (Wysolone 60 mg daily for 3 months) and azathioprine (Azoran 100 mg daily for the past 1 month), the patient presented with 2 months of progressive abdominal distension and generalized weakness and a 2-day acute illness marked by fever, productive cough, and purpuric rashes over both lower limbs.
subjective.past_medical_history: Autoimmune hepatitis with chronic liver disease (diagnosed 3 months prior), hypertension, hypothyroidism, and cholecystectomy 17 years prior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 2 months of abdominal distension and generalized weakness, and 2 days of fever, productive cough, and bilateral lower-extremity purpuric rash. Home medications: prednisolone (Wysolone) 60 mg daily, azathioprine (Azoran) 100 mg daily, antihypertensives, and thyroid hormone replacement.

objective.physical_examination: Initially conscious, oriented, and afebrile (subsequently developed altered sensorium and worsening respiratory failure requiring endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation); blood pressure 80/50 mmHg, pulse rate 118/min, respiratory rate 20/min; pallor, pedal edema, and palpable purpuric spots over both lower limbs; bilateral basal crepitations on chest auscultation; distended, tender abdomen with sluggish bowel sounds and paralytic ileus (nasogastric aspirate 600 mL/24h).
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 9.3 g/dL, total leukocyte count 8.9 x 10^9/L (83% neutrophils, 11% lymphocytes, 1% eosinophils), absolute eosinophil count 55/mm3 (ref 40-440), platelets 139 x 10^9/L, serum IgE 319 IU/mL (ref <100), CRP 144 mg/L, urea 120 mg/dL, creatinine 2.08 mg/dL, sodium 133 mmol/L, potassium 4.39 mmol/L, total bilirubin 1.4 mg/dL, AST 98 IU/L, ALT 82 IU/L, ALP 519 IU/L, GGT 800 IU/L, albumin 2.0 g/dL, and globulin 3.3 g/dL. ABG showed respiratory acidosis and hyperlactatemia (pH 7.30, pCO2 46 mmHg, pO2 87 mmHg, HCO3 20 mmol/L, lactate 3.2 mmol/L). Chest X-ray showed bilateral fluffy alveolar infiltrates, left-sided consolidation, and right ground-glass opacities; baseline TTE showed LVEF 50% without wall motion abnormalities (IVC 20 mm); abdominal ultrasound showed cirrhotic liver with irregular outline and coarse echotexture, minimal interloop ascites, and dilated fluid-filled small bowel loops with sluggish peristalsis.
objective.advanced_workup: Bronchial wash and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) cytology showed a hemorrhagic background, wet-mount microscopy demonstrated motile Strongyloides stercoralis larvae, and BAL bacterial culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae (other cultures sterile). Quantitative blood CMV DNA PCR was markedly elevated at 1.81 x 10^6 copies/mL. Lower-limb skin biopsy demonstrated dermal microvascular thrombi with RBC extravasation compatible with purpura fulminans (no larvae seen). Postmortem liver biopsy confirmed cirrhosis with sepsis features, and muscle biopsy showed focal muscle fiber atrophy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with fatal Strongyloides stercoralis hyperinfection syndrome complicated by high-level cytomegalovirus (CMV) viremia/co-infection (confirmed by quantitative CMV DNA PCR of 1.81 x 10^6/mL), Klebsiella pneumoniae ventilator/pulmonary co-infection, and purpura fulminans in a steroid- and azathioprine-immunosuppressed patient with autoimmune hepatitis cirrhosis. Managed with mechanical ventilation, high-dose vasopressor/inotropic support, sensitivity-guided intravenous antibiotics, and oral ivermectin (12 mg once daily); however, the patient suffered sudden cardiac arrest and could not be resuscitated.
